key_insight: Microscopic impurities nucleate perovskite degradation, and machine learning-supported optical imaging can rapidly flag films with elevated early-degradation risk.
engineering_relevance: Rapid, non-invasive impurity screening could support quality control for scalable fabrication of stable, wide-bandgap perovskite solar cells.
method: Identify impurities using nano-FTIR spectroscopy and high-resolution optical and scanning probe techniques.
Use photo-stress experiments to locate degradation onset at impurity–perovskite interfaces.
Detect and quantify impurities within seconds using reflected-light microscopy and machine learning-supported image analysis.
evidence_signal: Photo-stress experiments linked higher impurity density to faster early degradation, while degradation tracking indicated coupled photo- and thermo-chemical contributions.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative detection accuracy or validation across manufacturing conditions, leaving deployment robustness uncertain.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
